notes: Flagged large-source unit (לְ + מִן + רָחוֹק → long ago) reviewed and retained: the ASV writes one fixed adverbial expression for the whole phrase, no morpheme owns a part of it, and the subtraction test leaves nothing for either preposition on its own (rules 30, 40).
long ago is taken as one rendering of לְמֵרָחוֹק; the competing reading splits a word onto the prepositions, which the subtraction test does not support.
into was given to the head noun heaps rather than to the attributive it stands before; rule 33's positional wording is a heuristic and the noun is what the phrase turns on.
how answers to no conjunction in the Hebrew clause and is added (rule 55).
